one_line: A proof-carrying work layer where agents adversarially test human-owned definitions of done.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect a human-owned mission and acceptance contract, submit counterexamples to expose false-green criteria, and track evidence validity as dependencies change.
leverage_rationale: The claimed core interaction is an agent challenging acceptance contracts through structured WebMCP tools while semantic authority remains with the human; this is materially more precise and governable than an agent driving a generic dashboard, though the packet does not demonstrate it live.
leverage_evidence: About text names seven WebMCP tools including submit_counterexample, mission/authority/contract inspection, evidence inspection, and bounded human decisions.
The agent is explicitly barred from rewriting the contract, approving its own fix, or impersonating the human decision.
execution_rationale: The written concept is unusually coherent and detailed, but the packet has no video frames, transcript, or visible product interface; execution is therefore only plausibly real and cannot receive end-to-end credit.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows only written story packaging and no product UI, test output, or concrete counterexample run.
Facts report a live demo link but no submitted video or gallery images.
impact_rationale: Trustworthy completion and acceptance verification is a real problem for teams using agents, and the proposed human-authority and dependency-aware proof model addresses a specific failure mode; implementation value is not demonstrated in the packet.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies stale or incorrect definitions of done and false-green agent reports as the central trust problem.
Claims dependency changes invalidate only affected proof and produce a minimum re-proof plan.
creativity_rationale: The combination of human semantic authority, adversarial counterexamples, deterministic false-green detection, and selective re-proof is a fresh and ambitious interaction model for agent work assurance.
creativity_evidence: The agent actively attacks the human-owned acceptance contract instead of merely executing it.
The concept distinguishes mission authority, contract defects, execution evidence, and dependency-scoped proof validity.
usability_note: The intended human/agent roles are clearly articulated, but no interface or demonstrated workflow is available to assess operational usability.
red_flags: No visual or end-to-end evidence despite broad functional claims.
Demo is reported alive, but the packet supplies no observed run or implementation detail.
standouts: Strong separation of human semantic authority from agent testing authority.
Selective invalidation and minimum re-proof plan are a compelling trust model.
advance_reason: The concept and WebMCP interaction are strong enough to advance, but execution and eligibility require live verification.

one_line: A shadow-theatre trial where human changes invalidate stale agent plans atomically.
what_it_does: Provides a shared visual scene in which a human owns the lamp and capability grants while an agent observes, measures, plans, and controls a bounded shadow rig; stale plans are rejected after human state changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is presented as the coordination layer for live transient browser state, typed observation/measurement/planning/commit tools, revision checks, and explicit authority boundaries. A generic UI-driving agent would be substantially less reliable at detecting and safely rejecting the race.
leverage_evidence: The packet describes a live human override producing LAMP_SEQUENCE_CONFLICT, zero partial mutations, and SAFE_RECOVERY.
Frame sheets visibly label native WebMCP, human-owned authority, stale-plan rejection, zero mutations, and reread/remeasure/rebuild recovery.
The agent is limited to a four-piece shadow rig and cannot move the human-owned lamp or grant itself permission.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent, intentionally staged workflow and visible state transitions from human change through stale-plan rejection to recovery. Exact enforcement and successful agent invocation are not fully readable, so this stops short of a 9-10.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show consistent UI, scene state, authority controls, revision-bound planning, and the LAMP SEQUENCE CONFLICT path.
Frames explicitly state zero mutations/zero partial damage and require reread, remeasure, and rebuild.
Devpost screenshot includes an embedded demo preview with reality authority, current phase, and live ledger panels.
impact_rationale: The project addresses a concrete safety and reliability problem for human-agent collaboration: humans change shared state while agents operate. The bounded authority and atomic rejection model has credible value for agentic interfaces, even though the visual theatre is a focused demonstration.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on stale plans caused by real human edits and safe recovery without partial mutations.
The demo visibly communicates a reproducible race-condition trial and exportable evidence ledger.
creativity_rationale: The shadow-theatre framing turns a difficult concurrency and authority problem into a memorable visual interaction, while pursuing it deeply through live state, bounded capabilities, revision-bound plans, and evidence capsules.
creativity_evidence: The product uses a four-piece shadow rig and human-controlled lamp as an unusual but legible model of shared reality.
The interaction model makes stale-plan races visible rather than hiding them behind generic agent automation.
Frame captions and UI consistently develop the human-authority/recovery narrative.
usability_note: The staged flow and visible authority/status cues make the intended workflow understandable; small text and a specialized metaphor may limit practical accessibility outside the demo context.
red_flags: Contact sheets and screenshot do not independently prove the underlying native-WebMCP/no-hidden-API claims.
Agent invocation details and exact event ledger contents are too small to verify fully.
standouts: Clear atomic stale-plan rejection with zero partial mutations.
Strong separation of human-owned reality from agent-owned bounded controls.
Memorable visual demonstration of a real concurrency problem.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage, coherent demonstrated workflow, and unusually original treatment of shared-state recovery warrant advancement.
